proposed_additions.question: How are Faction Mats and Player Mats assigned, and in what relative faction order should players sit? Why does that seating matter for recruit bonuses?
proposed_additions.expected_answer: Randomly shuffle the Faction Mats and Player Mats and deal one of each to each player. Players sit near their faction home bases, with the clockwise order from the top Nordic, Rusviet, Crimea, Saxony, Polania, using the factions in the game. Recruit ongoing bonuses respond to the player and their immediate left/right neighbors, so those neighbors follow the seating arrangement.
proposed_additions.novelty: Distinct setup selection and required relative seating procedure. Q01 asks Factory/encounter/structure setup and start player; Q02 asks piece placement and starting values; Q12 assumes already established left/right neighbors. None elicits or keys mat assignment or seating.

proposed_additions.question: For movement, what distinguishes a river from a lake, and from which surrounding land territories can a unit with a lake-movement ability enter the lake?
proposed_additions.expected_answer: A river lies on the border between two land territories. A lake comprises an entire territory hex and extends from that hex to any adjacent shoreline. A unit with the appropriate lake-movement ability can move onto it from any of the surrounding territories shown by that shoreline; crossing permission for a river alone does not grant entry to lakes.

source_references.heading: RIVERS AND LAKES; RIVER; LAKE; illustrated example

proposed_additions.novelty: Distinct source-defined map adjacency rule, rather than another example of the already tested faction ability permissions. Q27/Q33 distinguish abilities and destinations but do not define the geographic boundary or surrounding-shoreline adjacency used to apply those abilities.
